rootNote: Teaching root chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126): H5975 עָמַד is the most frequent I-Guttural root with no second weakness (518 verb tokens: Qal 433, Hiphil 83, Hophal 2). It is also the paradigm root of GKC §63 / Paradigm D and Davidson §34. It has no Niphal, Piel, Pual or Hitpael in the Bible, so those squares take examples from other I-Guttural roots (and I-Aleph roots where א behaves as a guttural).
source: Forms from GKC §63 + Paradigm D (Verbs primae gutturalis) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §34 paradigm (pp. 170-171), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/. Squares those tables do not print (Piel, Pual, Hitpael, some person forms) follow GKC §63 (only forms where the first radical is affected deviate) applied to the strong-verb.json pattern; formBasis says which ('book' = printed in GKC or Davidson; 'rule' = regular pattern). Not copied from any copyrighted chart. Where K&J (the BBH stand-in) prints a square we had built by rule, the K&J form is used with formBasis 'printed'; K&J's -ָה feminine participles are 'printed' alternates (tutor rulings 2026-11-21 4:09 PM ET; see tools/kj_rulings.py).
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective holam, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot. Radicals are positional (R1 = ע, R2 = מ, R3 = ד); a begadkefat radical's dagesh in dagesh-lene position is optional. The example's root (with shin/sin dot) was checked against the Strong's headword for its lemma number. Example roots: 1st radical א ה ח ע; 2nd radical not guttural/ר/ו/י; 3rd not guttural/ר/א/ה/ו/י/נ; not geminate; הלך and the five quiescent I-Aleph verbs (אבד אבה אכל אמר אפה, GKC §68.1) excluded. Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition (examplePrefix). Example preference: teaching root, then another I-Guttural root (ה ח ע), then an I-Aleph root behaving as a guttural; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.cohortative: Cohortative = 1st-person yiqtol + ָה: Qal אֶעֶמְדָה, Hiphil אַעֲמִידָה (Davidson p. 170-171). Shown as a note, not a table row.
notes.jussive: As in the strong verb, the jussive looks like yiqtol except in Hiphil (יַעֲמֵד vs יַעֲמִיד).
notes.weqatal: Qal וְעָמַדְתָּ (Davidson p. 170); Hiphil after wāw consecutive וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ (GKC §63.2 Rem. (3)). Shown as a note, not a column.
notes.qalStativeType: Stative verbs take a different Qal yiqtol: יֶחֱזַק, תֶּחֶזְקִי, יֶחֶזְקוּ, imperative חֲזַק (GKC Paradigm D second Qal column; Davidson p. 170 'stat.'). Not built as cells.
notes.hardCombination: Some roots (often with ח) close the syllable instead of using a ḥaṭeph: יַחְמֹד, יַחְשֹׁב, יֶחְבַּשׁ (GKC §63.2(a),(c)). These vowel patterns differ from the chart and are not used as examples.
notes.gutturalRules: Rules: (1) a guttural takes ḥaṭeph instead of vocal shewa (GKC §63.1); (2) after a preformative the guttural repeats the preformative vowel as ḥaṭeph, pataḥ in Qal/Hiphil yiqtol, seghol in Niphal/Hiphil qatal, qameṣ ḥaṭuf in Hophal (§63.2); (3) before a vocal ending the ḥaṭeph becomes a full short vowel (§63.3); (4) the guttural cannot be doubled, so Niphal yiqtol/imperative/infinitive lengthen the preformative to ṣere (§63.4). Piel, Pual and Hitpael are regular.
notes.iAleph: I-Aleph: where א keeps its consonant value it behaves as here, but with ḥaṭeph seghol (אֱכֹל, נֶאֱסַף; GKC §63 Remarks on Qal, 1). Five verbs make א quiesce in Qal yiqtol: אָבַד, אָבָה, אָכַל, אָמַר, אָפָה → יֹאכַל, וַיֹּאמֶר (GKC §68.1; Davidson §35). Those are not on this chart.
notes.Hophal imperative: None: GKC Paradigm D and Davidson p. 171 mark it 'wanting'.
